- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.10) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices after strong negative sentiment spikes (sentiment < -0.30) — adjust downward bias by 2–5%.
- Overshoot after recent price spikes — cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below prior high.
- Mean-reversion bias: if 3+ consecutive forecast days exceed true outcome by >5%, reduce next forecast by 3–7%.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment was positive 3–5 days prior, forecast should be slightly lower than model output.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate early in cycle — reduce first 5–7 days by 2–4% if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, reduce forecast by 5–10% across all horizon.
